native_result.HypoA: The least used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects are ML Canvas (10.13% respondents, 95% CI [9.926, 10.333]) and Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) Scenarios (4.366% respondents, 95% CI [4.231, 4.501]) after bootstrapping for statistical significance.
native_result.HypoB: ML Canvas and BDD scenarios are the two least-used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects. In the Q10 documentation multi-select battery, answered by 194 of the 276 stored respondents (82 non-responders, all 'Suspended', coded -77 and dropped as NA rather than counted as zeros), ML Canvas was used by 15/194 = 7.73% of respondents (95% bootstrap percentile CI 4.12-11.86; Wilson 4.74-12.36) and BDD scenarios by 4/194 = 2.06% (CI 0.52-4.12; Wilson 0.81-5.18) - the two lowest of the ten named formats, versus Notebooks 34.02%, User Stories 32.47% and Requirements Lists 26.29%. Respondent-level bootstrap (20,000 replicates) makes BDD scenarios the least-used format in 99.9% of replicates and ML Canvas the second least-used in 97.5% of replicates among named formats; the ordering is unchanged on all 276 rows (5.43%/1.45%), Completed-only (8.0%/2.13%), respondents naming at least one format (10.27%/2.74%) and under project-count weighting. ML Canvas counts as second-least because the 'Other' free-text option is treated as an unspecified residual rather than a format: it ties ML Canvas at 15/194 and keeping it splits the second-least probability 54%/46%; its 14 free texts (Confluence/Jira/Notion/wiki pages, design documents, meeting notes, mathematical models) contain no alias for any named format, and 'Not Documented' (15.46%) is excluded because it denotes absent documentation, not a format. Our replication is consistent with those figures in the identity and ordering of the two least-used formats (ML Canvas ahead of BDD scenarios, the absolute minimum), while our respondent-level percentages are lower.
